learned_patterns.pattern: The Signal Engine has now been down ~10 days (last run 06-30 12:21 PDT), forcing continuous SAFE MODE. A recurring scheduled-run miss has escalated into a sustained outage. The §2.5 guard correctly prevented trading on decade-stale signals, but the book has been unable to act on any new setup for ten days. Engine cron/runner reliability is the top operational risk, ahead of signal quality.

INTC — the highest-ATR LAB name (7.6% ATR, 12.6% stop) and the flagged SOXX-transition candidate — eventually broke its stop and exited -14.98% on 07-07 after topping near $142. The tight-vs-wide ATR stop debate resolved: even a wide 12.6% stop on a high-vol single name gave back the entire gain. Reinforces the §13.3 thesis of migrating single-name semis into SOXX to cut idiosyncratic drawdown.

NVDA carried a composite -0.338 BEARISH / Trend50=Down on the 06-30 matrix yet rallied +8% over the following days to sit +11% above its stop. In sharp reversals the composite's Bearish MACD term lags price badly and misreads recovering names. Confirms the earlier medium-confidence pattern: the composite is a lagging confirmation, not a leading signal — never exit a held name on a bearish composite alone (and CLU does not).

An involuntary exit (INTC stop-out) did the rebalancing that deposit-routing could not: it pulled LAB 25.9% -> 18.0%, back under the 20% cap, and freed $10.63 of redeployment capital. Organic exits are the §17.3-sanctioned way an overweight tier normalizes — no force-selling required. The book self-corrected toward its glide path via the stop loop.

Dividend yields still render sanely (JEPQ 9.95%, JEPI 8.10%, SCHD 3.30%) but dividend_growth_streak=0 and payout_ratio=null persist for every DRIP name, so the §15.3 growth screen stays unverifiable. Covered-call JEPI/JEPQ (payout N/A by rule) can seed on yield; SCHD/DGRO/VIG/VYM remain blocked on the fix. Unchanged since 06-30.
